Fig. 4 shows the ranging RMSE versus distance for different modulation constellations and the communication BER versus distance for downlink and uplink channels. reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed bidirectional RO-ISAC system uses time division duplexing (TDD) and clipped orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) to achieve simultaneous communication and sensing. The system consists of a downlink device and an uplink device, where the uplink device uses a corner cube reflector (CCR) to reflect the downlink signal back to the downlink device for passive ranging. The TDD-based interference cancellation scheme is used to avoid interference between the reflected downlink signal and the uplink signal.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports a ranging resolution of 6 cm and a maximum ranging distance of 96 cm. The communication bit error ratio (BER) is below the 7% forward error correction (FEC) coding threshold of 3.8 × 10^(-3) for a distance of 96 cm. The overall data rate is also reported for different maximum ranging distances using fixed and adaptive guard intervals (GIs).

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed bidirectional RO-ISAC system solves the problem of achieving simultaneous communication and sensing using a single waveform. However, the system's performance is affected by the clipping ratio of the OFDM signal, which has a different impact on communication and ranging performance. The paper also highlights the importance of adaptive GI in improving the overall data rate of the system.
